calls.head: The Blue Jackets like Coyle’s line against Karlsson’s
calls.body: At home, the Blue Jackets keep sending Coyle’s line (Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier) out against opponents’ second lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rick Bowness keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Golden Knights’ second line is Howden, Karlsson and Holtz.

CBJ.head: We had Columbus as slight underdogs (42%), and they pulled it off.

VGK.head: We leaned Vegas’s way (58%), but Columbus had other ideas.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Fantilli ends it in overtime
paras: Denton Mateychuk struck first for the Blue Jackets midway through the first, but Tomáš Hertl tied it 1-1 for Vegas late in the period. Adam Fantilli won it on the power play 59 seconds into overtime.

The Golden Knights had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Golden Knights win about six in ten. Cam Talbot was the difference, stopping 26 of 27. Carter Hart stopped 18 of 20 for the Golden Knights. The Blue Jackets moved to 4-5-0, still last in the Metropolitan, while the Knights dropped to 8-4-1, second in the Pacific.

items.text: The Blue Jackets scored on the power play for the first time since Oct 1, after going 0-for-20 over seven games.
The Golden Knights are winless in three (0-2-1).
The Blue Jackets bounced back after two straight losses.
Emil Andrae faces his old team, Philadelphia, on Tuesday.
